# convert_case - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/convert_case/^0.6/

## Expand description

Converts to and from various cases.

This library was developed for the purposes of a command line utility for converting
the case of strings and filenames.  You can check out
[ ccase on Github](https://github.com/rutrum/convert-case/tree/master/ccase).

Provides a [ Case](https://docs.rs/enum.Case.html) enum which defines a variety of cases to convert into.
Strings have implemented the

[trait, which adds methods for case conversion.](https://docs.rs/trait.Casing.html)

`Casing`You can convert strings into a case using the [ to_case](https://docs.rs/trait.Casing.html#tymethod.to_case) method.

```
use convert_case::{Case, Casing};
assert_eq!("Ronnie James Dio", "ronnie james dio".to_case(Case::Title));
assert_eq!("ronnieJamesDio", "Ronnie_James_dio".to_case(Case::Camel));
assert_eq!("Ronnie-James-Dio", "RONNIE_JAMES_DIO".to_case(Case::Train));
```
By default, `to_case` will split along a set of default word boundaries, that is

- space characters - underscores `_`,
- hyphens `-`,
- changes in capitalization from lowercase to uppercase `aA`,
- adjacent digits and letters `a1`,`1a`,`A1`,`1A`,
- and acroynms `AAa`(as in`HTTPRequest`).

For more accuracy, the `from_case` method splits based on the word boundaries
of a particular case.  For example, splitting from snake case will only use
underscores as word boundaries.

```
use convert_case::{Case, Casing};
assert_eq!(
    "2020 04 16 My Cat Cali",
    "2020-04-16_my_cat_cali".to_case(Case::Title)
);
assert_eq!(
    "2020-04-16 My Cat Cali",
    "2020-04-16_my_cat_cali".from_case(Case::Snake).to_case(Case::Title)
);
```
Case conversion can detect acronyms for camel-like strings. It also ignores any leading, trailing, or duplicate delimiters.

```
use convert_case::{Case, Casing};
assert_eq!("io_stream", "IOStream".to_case(Case::Snake));
assert_eq!("my_json_parser", "myJSONParser".to_case(Case::Snake));
assert_eq!("weird_var_name", "__weird--var _name-".to_case(Case::Snake));
```
It also works non-ascii characters.  However, no inferences on the language itself is made.
For instance, the digraph `ij` in Dutch will not be capitalized, because it is represented
as two distinct Unicode characters.  However, `æ` would be capitalized.  Accuracy with unicode
characters is done using the `unicode-segmentation` crate, the sole dependency of this crate.

```
use convert_case::{Case, Casing};
assert_eq!("granat-äpfel", "GranatÄpfel".to_case(Case::Kebab));
assert_eq!("Перспектива 24", "ПЕРСПЕКТИВА24".to_case(Case::Title));
// The example from str::to_lowercase documentation
let odysseus = "ὈΔΥΣΣΕΎΣ";
assert_eq!("ὀδυσσεύς", odysseus.to_case(Case::Lower));
```
By default, characters followed by digits and vice-versa are
considered word boundaries.  In addition, any special ASCII characters (besides `_` and `-`)
are ignored.

```
use convert_case::{Case, Casing};
assert_eq!("e_5150", "E5150".to_case(Case::Snake));
assert_eq!("10,000_days", "10,000Days".to_case(Case::Snake));
assert_eq!("HELLO, WORLD!", "Hello, world!".to_case(Case::Upper));
assert_eq!("One\ntwo\nthree", "ONE\nTWO\nTHREE".to_case(Case::Title));
```
You can also test what case a string is in.

```
use convert_case::{Case, Casing};
assert!( "css-class-name".is_case(Case::Kebab));
assert!(!"css-class-name".is_case(Case::Snake));
assert!(!"UPPER_CASE_VAR".is_case(Case::Snake));
```
The `Casing` methods `from_case` and `to_case` do not fail.  Conversion to a case will always
succeed.  However, the results can still be unexpected.  Failure to detect any word boundaries
for a particular case means the entire string will be considered a single word.

```
use convert_case::{Case, Casing};
// Mistakenly parsing using Case::Snake
assert_eq!("My-kebab-var", "my-kebab-var".from_case(Case::Snake).to_case(Case::Title));
// Converts using an unexpected method
assert_eq!("my_kebab_like_variable", "myKebab-like-variable".to_case(Case::Snake));
```
It can be difficult to determine how to split a string into words.  That is why this case
provides the [ from_case](https://docs.rs/trait.Casing.html#tymethod.from_case) functionality, but sometimes that isn’t enough
to meet a specific use case.

Take an identifier has the word `2D`, such as `scale2D`.  No exclusive usage of `from_case` will
be enough to solve the problem.  In this case we can further specify which boundaries to split
the string on.  `convert_case` provides some patterns for achieving this specificity.
We can specify what boundaries we want to split on using the [ Boundary enum](https://docs.rs/enum.Boundary.html).

```
use convert_case::{Boundary, Case, Casing};
// Not quite what we want
assert_eq!(
    "scale_2_d",
    "scale2D"
        .from_case(Case::Camel)
        .to_case(Case::Snake)
);
// Remove boundary from Case::Camel
assert_eq!(
    "scale_2d",
    "scale2D"
        .from_case(Case::Camel)
        .without_boundaries(&[Boundary::DigitUpper, Boundary::DigitLower])
        .to_case(Case::Snake)
);
// Write boundaries explicitly
assert_eq!(
    "scale_2d",
    "scale2D"
        .with_boundaries(&[Boundary::LowerDigit])
        .to_case(Case::Snake)
);
```
The `Casing` trait provides initial methods, but any subsequent methods that do not resolve
the conversion return a [ StateConverter](https://docs.rs/struct.StateConverter.html) struct.  It contains similar methods as

`Casing`.Because `Case` is an enum, you can’t create your own variant for your use case.  However
the parameters for case conversion have been encapsulated into the [ Converter](https://docs.rs/struct.Converter.html) struct
which can be used for specific use cases.

Suppose you wanted to format a word like camel case, where the first word is lower case and the
rest are capitalized.  But you want to include a delimeter like underscore.  This case isn’t
available as a `Case` variant, but you can create it by constructing the parameters of the
`Converter`.

```
use convert_case::{Case, Casing, Converter, Pattern};
let conv = Converter::new()
    .set_pattern(Pattern::Camel)
    .set_delim("_");
assert_eq!(
    "my_Special_Case",
    conv.convert("My Special Case")
)
```
Just as with the `Casing` trait, you can also manually set the boundaries strings are split
on.  You can use any of the [ Pattern](https://docs.rs/enum.Pattern.html) variants available.  This even includes

[which isn’t used in any](https://docs.rs/enum.Pattern.html#variant.Sentence)

`Pattern::Sentence``Case` variant.  You can also set no pattern at all, which will
maintain the casing of each letter in the input string.  You can also, of course, set any string as your
delimeter.For more details on how strings are converted, see the docs for [ Converter](https://docs.rs/struct.Converter.html).

To ensure this library had zero dependencies, randomness was moved to the *random* feature,
which requires the `rand` crate. You can enable this feature by including the
following in your `Cargo.toml`.

```
[dependencies]
convert_case = { version = "^0.3.0", features = ["random"] }
```
This will add two additional cases: Random and PseudoRandom.  You can read about their
construction in the [Case enum](https://docs.rs/enum.Case.html).

A boundary defines how a string is split into words.  Some boundaries, `Hyphen`, `Underscore`,
and `Space`, consume the character they split on, whereas the other boundaries
do not.

---

# proc_macro2 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/^1.0/

## Expand description

A wrapper around the procedural macro API of the compiler’s [ proc_macro](https://doc.rust-lang.org/proc_macro/index.html)
crate. This library serves two purposes:

-
**Bring proc-macro-like functionality to other contexts like build.rs and main.rs.**Types from`proc_macro`are entirely specific to procedural macros and cannot ever exist in code outside of a procedural macro. Meanwhile`proc_macro2`types may exist anywhere including non-macro code. By developing foundational libraries like[syn](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn)and[quote](https://github.com/dtolnay/quote)against`proc_macro2`rather than`proc_macro`, the procedural macro ecosystem becomes easily applicable to many other use cases and we avoid reimplementing non-macro equivalents of those libraries.
-
**Make procedural macros unit testable.**As a consequence of being specific to procedural macros, nothing that uses`proc_macro`can be executed from a unit test. In order for helper libraries or components of a macro to be testable in isolation, they must be implemented using`proc_macro2`.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

The skeleton of a typical procedural macro typically looks like this:

```
extern crate proc_macro;
#[proc_macro_derive(MyDerive)]
pub fn my_derive(input: proc_macro::TokenStream) -> proc_macro::TokenStream {
    let input = proc_macro2::TokenStream::from(input);
    let output: proc_macro2::TokenStream = {
        /* transform input */
    };
    proc_macro::TokenStream::from(output)
}
```
If parsing with [Syn](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn), you’ll use [ parse_macro_input!](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0/syn/macro.parse_macro_input.html) instead to
propagate parse errors correctly back to the compiler when parsing fails.

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable features

The default feature set of proc-macro2 tracks the most recent stable
compiler API. Functionality in `proc_macro` that is not yet stable is not
exposed by proc-macro2 by default.

To opt into the additional APIs available in the most recent nightly
compiler, the `procmacro2_semver_exempt` config flag must be passed to
rustc. We will polyfill those nightly-only APIs back to Rust 1.68.0. As
these are unstable APIs that track the nightly compiler, minor versions of
proc-macro2 may make breaking changes to them at any time.

`RUSTFLAGS='--cfg procmacro2_semver_exempt' cargo build`Note that this must not only be done for your crate, but for any crate that depends on your crate. This infectious nature is intentional, as it serves as a reminder that you are outside of the normal semver guarantees.

Semver exempt methods are marked as such in the proc-macro2 documentation.

[§](https://docs.rs#thread-safety)Thread-Safety

Most types in this crate are `!Sync` because the underlying compiler
types make use of thread-local memory, meaning they cannot be accessed from
a different thread.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [extra](https://docs.rs/extra/index.html)
- Items which do not have a correspondence to any API in the proc_macro crate, but are necessary to include in proc-macro2.
- [token_](https://docs.rs/token_stream/index.html)- stream
- Public implementation details for the `TokenStream`type, such as iterators.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Group](https://docs.rs/struct.Group.html)
- A delimited token stream.
- [Ident](https://docs.rs/struct.Ident.html)
- A word of Rust code, which may be a keyword or legal variable name.
- [LexError](https://docs.rs/struct.LexError.html)
- Error returned from `TokenStream::from_str`.
- [Line](https://docs.rs/struct.LineColumn.html)- Column - `span-locations`
- A line-column pair representing the start or end of a `Span`.
- [Literal](https://docs.rs/struct.Literal.html)
- A literal string (`"hello"`), byte string (`b"hello"`), character (`'a'`), byte character (`b'a'`), an integer or floating point number with or without a suffix (`1`,`1u8`,`2.3`,`2.3f32`).
- [Punct](https://docs.rs/struct.Punct.html)
- A `Punct`is a single punctuation character like`+`,`-`or`#`.
- [Span](https://docs.rs/struct.Span.html)
- A region of source code, along with macro expansion information.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/struct.TokenStream.html)- Stream
- An abstract stream of tokens, or more concretely a sequence of token trees.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Conversion](https://docs.rs/enum.ConversionErrorKind.html)- Error - Kind - `procmacro2_semver_exempt`
- Error when retrieving a string literal’s unescaped value.
- [Delimiter](https://docs.rs/enum.Delimiter.html)
- Describes how a sequence of token trees is delimited.
- [Escape](https://docs.rs/enum.EscapeError.html)- Error - `procmacro2_semver_exempt`
- Errors and warnings that can occur during string, char, and byte unescaping.
- [Spacing](https://docs.rs/enum.Spacing.html)
- Whether a `Punct`is followed immediately by another`Punct`or followed by another token or whitespace.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/enum.TokenTree.html)- Tree
- A single token or a delimited sequence of token trees (e.g. `[1, (), ..]`).

---

# quote - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/quote/^1.0/

## Expand description

This crate provides the [ quote!](https://docs.rs/macro.quote.html) macro for turning Rust syntax tree data
structures into tokens of source code.

Procedural macros in Rust receive a stream of tokens as input, execute arbitrary Rust code to determine how to manipulate those tokens, and produce a stream of tokens to hand back to the compiler to compile into the caller’s crate. Quasi-quoting is a solution to one piece of that — producing tokens to return to the compiler.

The idea of quasi-quoting is that we write *code* that we treat as *data*.
Within the `quote!` macro, we can write what looks like code to our text
editor or IDE. We get all the benefits of the editor’s brace matching,
syntax highlighting, indentation, and maybe autocompletion. But rather than
compiling that as code into the current crate, we can treat it as data, pass
it around, mutate it, and eventually hand it back to the compiler as tokens
to compile into the macro caller’s crate.

This crate is motivated by the procedural macro use case, but is a general-purpose Rust quasi-quoting library and is not specific to procedural macros.

```
[dependencies]
quote = "1.0"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

The following quasi-quoted block of code is something you might find in [a](https://serde.rs/)
procedural macro having to do with data structure serialization. The `#var`
syntax performs interpolation of runtime variables into the quoted tokens.
Check out the documentation of the [ quote!](https://docs.rs/macro.quote.html) macro for more detail about
the syntax. See also the

[macro which is important for implementing hygienic procedural macros.](https://docs.rs/macro.quote_spanned.html)

`quote_spanned!````
let tokens = quote! {
    struct SerializeWith #generics #where_clause {
        value: &'a #field_ty,
        phantom: core::marker::PhantomData<#item_ty>,
    }
    impl #generics serde::Serialize for SerializeWith #generics #where_clause {
        fn serialize<S>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error>
        where
            S: serde::Serializer,
        {
            #path(self.value, serializer)
        }
    }
    SerializeWith {
        value: #value,
        phantom: core::marker::PhantomData::<#item_ty>,
    }
};
```
[§](https://docs.rs#non-macro-code-generators)Non-macro code generators

When using `quote` in a build.rs or main.rs and writing the output out to a
file, consider having the code generator pass the tokens through
[prettyplease](https://github.com/dtolnay/prettyplease) before writing. This way if an error occurs in the generated
code it is convenient for a human to read and debug.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [format_](https://docs.rs/macro.format_ident.html)- ident
- Formatting macro for constructing `Ident`s.
- [quote](https://docs.rs/macro.quote.html)
- The whole point.
- [quote_](https://docs.rs/macro.quote_spanned.html)- spanned
- Same as `quote!`, but applies a given span to all tokens originating within the macro invocation.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Ident](https://docs.rs/trait.IdentFragment.html)- Fragment
- Specialized formatting trait used by `format_ident!`.
- [ToTokens](https://docs.rs/trait.ToTokens.html)
- Types that can be interpolated inside a `quote!`invocation.
- [Token](https://docs.rs/trait.TokenStreamExt.html)- Stream - Ext
- TokenStream extension trait with methods for appending tokens.

---

# syn - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/syn/^2.0/

## Expand description

Syn is a parsing library for parsing a stream of Rust tokens into a syntax tree of Rust source code.

Currently this library is geared toward use in Rust procedural macros, but contains some APIs that may be useful more generally.

-
**Data structures**— Syn provides a complete syntax tree that can represent any valid Rust source code. The syntax tree is rooted at`syn::File``syn::Item``syn::Expr``syn::Type`
-
**Derives**— Of particular interest to derive macros is`syn::DeriveInput`
-
**Parsing**— Parsing in Syn is built around[parser functions](https://docs.rs/parse/index.html)with the signature`fn(ParseStream) -> Result<T>`. Every syntax tree node defined by Syn is individually parsable and may be used as a building block for custom syntaxes, or you may dream up your own brand new syntax without involving any of our syntax tree types.
-
**Location information**— Every token parsed by Syn is associated with a`Span`that tracks line and column information back to the source of that token. These spans allow a procedural macro to display detailed error messages pointing to all the right places in the user’s code. There is an example of this below.
-
**Feature flags**— Functionality is aggressively feature gated so your procedural macros enable only what they need, and do not pay in compile time for all the rest.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-of-a-derive-macro)Example of a derive macro

The canonical derive macro using Syn looks like this. We write an ordinary
Rust function tagged with a `proc_macro_derive` attribute and the name of
the trait we are deriving. Any time that derive appears in the user’s code,
the Rust compiler passes their data structure as tokens into our macro. We
get to execute arbitrary Rust code to figure out what to do with those
tokens, then hand some tokens back to the compiler to compile into the
user’s crate.

```
[dependencies]
syn = "2.0"
quote = "1.0"
[lib]
proc-macro = true
```
```
use proc_macro::TokenStream;
use quote::quote;
use syn::{parse_macro_input, DeriveInput};
#[proc_macro_derive(MyMacro)]
pub fn my_macro(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
    // Parse the input tokens into a syntax tree
    let input = parse_macro_input!(input as DeriveInput);
    // Build the output, possibly using quasi-quotation
    let expanded = quote! {
        // ...
    };
    // Hand the output tokens back to the compiler
    TokenStream::from(expanded)
}
```
The [ heapsize](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn/tree/master/examples/heapsize) example directory shows a complete working implementation
of a derive macro. The example derives a

`HeapSize` trait which computes an
estimate of the amount of heap memory owned by a value.```
pub trait HeapSize {
    /// Total number of bytes of heap memory owned by `self`.
    fn heap_size_of_children(&self) -> usize;
}
```
The derive macro allows users to write `#[derive(HeapSize)]` on data
structures in their program.

```
#[derive(HeapSize)]
struct Demo<'a, T: ?Sized> {
    a: Box<T>,
    b: u8,
    c: &'a str,
    d: String,
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#spans-and-error-reporting)Spans and error reporting

The token-based procedural macro API provides great control over where the
compiler’s error messages are displayed in user code. Consider the error the
user sees if one of their field types does not implement `HeapSize`.

```
#[derive(HeapSize)]
struct Broken {
    ok: String,
    bad: std::thread::Thread,
}
```
By tracking span information all the way through the expansion of a
procedural macro as shown in the `heapsize` example, token-based macros in
Syn are able to trigger errors that directly pinpoint the source of the
problem.

```
error[E0277]: the trait bound `std::thread::Thread: HeapSize` is not satisfied
 --> src/main.rs:7:5
  |
7 |     bad: std::thread::Thread,
  |     ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the trait `HeapSize` is not implemented for `Thread`
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parsing-a-custom-syntax)Parsing a custom syntax

The [ lazy-static](https://github.com/dtolnay/syn/tree/master/examples/lazy-static) example directory shows the implementation of a

`functionlike!(...)` procedural macro in which the input tokens are parsed
using Syn’s parsing API.The example reimplements the popular `lazy_static` crate from crates.io as a
procedural macro.

```
lazy_static! {
    static ref USERNAME: Regex = Regex::new("^[a-z0-9_-]{3,16}$").unwrap();
}
```
The implementation shows how to trigger custom warnings and error messages on the macro input.

```
warning: come on, pick a more creative name
  --> src/main.rs:10:16
   |
10 |     static ref FOO: String = "lazy_static".to_owned();
   |                ^^^
```
[§](https://docs.rs#testing)Testing

When testing macros, we often care not just that the macro can be used
successfully but also that when the macro is provided with invalid input it
produces maximally helpful error messages. Consider using the [ trybuild](https://github.com/dtolnay/trybuild)
crate to write tests for errors that are emitted by your macro or errors
detected by the Rust compiler in the expanded code following misuse of the
macro. Such tests help avoid regressions from later refactors that
mistakenly make an error no longer trigger or be less helpful than it used
to be.

[§](https://docs.rs#debugging)Debugging

When developing a procedural macro it can be helpful to look at what the
generated code looks like. Use `cargo rustc -- -Zunstable-options -Zunpretty=expanded` or the [ cargo expand](https://github.com/dtolnay/cargo-expand) subcommand.

To show the expanded code for some crate that uses your procedural macro,
run `cargo expand` from that crate. To show the expanded code for one of
your own test cases, run `cargo expand --test the_test_case` where the last
argument is the name of the test file without the `.rs` extension.

This write-up by Brandon W Maister discusses debugging in more detail:
[Debugging Rust’s new Custom Derive system](https://quodlibetor.github.io/posts/debugging-rusts-new-custom-derive-system/).

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional features

Syn puts a lot of functionality behind optional features in order to optimize compile time for the most common use cases. The following features are available.

- `derive`- *(enabled by default)*— Data structures for representing the possible input to a derive macro, including structs and enums and types.
- `full`
- `parsing`- *(enabled by default)*— Ability to parse input tokens into a syntax tree node of a chosen type.
- `printing`- *(enabled by default)*— Ability to print a syntax tree node as tokens of Rust source code.
- `visit`
- `visit-mut`
- `fold`
- `clone-impls`- *(enabled by default)*— Clone impls for all syntax tree types.
- `extra-traits`
- `proc-macro`- *(enabled by default)*— Runtime dependency on the dynamic library libproc_macro from rustc toolchain.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [buffer](https://docs.rs/buffer/index.html)- `parsing`
- A stably addressed token buffer supporting efficient traversal based on a cheaply copyable cursor.
- [ext](https://docs.rs/ext/index.html)
- Extension traits to provide parsing methods on foreign types.
- [fold](https://docs.rs/fold/index.html)- `fold`
- Syntax tree traversal to transform the nodes of an owned syntax tree.
- [meta](https://docs.rs/meta/index.html)- `parsing`and (- `derive`or- `full`)
- Facility for interpreting structured content inside of an `Attribute`.
- [parse](https://docs.rs/parse/index.html)- `parsing`
- Parsing interface for parsing a token stream into a syntax tree node.
- [punctuated](https://docs.rs/punctuated/index.html)
- A punctuated sequence of syntax tree nodes separated by punctuation.
- [spanned](https://docs.rs/spanned/index.html)- `parsing`and- `printing`
- A trait that can provide the `Span`of the complete contents of a syntax tree node.
- [token](https://docs.rs/token/index.html)
- Tokens representing Rust punctuation, keywords, and delimiters.
- [visit](https://docs.rs/visit/index.html)- `visit`
- Syntax tree traversal to walk a shared borrow of a syntax tree.
- [visit_](https://docs.rs/visit_mut/index.html)- mut - `visit-mut`
- Syntax tree traversal to mutate an exclusive borrow of a syntax tree in place.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [Token](https://docs.rs/macro.Token.html)
- A type-macro that expands to the name of the Rust type representation of a given token.
- [braced](https://docs.rs/macro.braced.html)- `parsing`
- Parse a set of curly braces and expose their content to subsequent parsers.
- [bracketed](https://docs.rs/macro.bracketed.html)- `parsing`
- Parse a set of square brackets and expose their content to subsequent parsers.
- [custom_](https://docs.rs/macro.custom_keyword.html)- keyword
- Define a type that supports parsing and printing a given identifier as if it were a keyword.
- [custom_](https://docs.rs/macro.custom_punctuation.html)- punctuation
- Define a type that supports parsing and printing a multi-character symbol as if it were a punctuation token.
- [parenthesized](https://docs.rs/macro.parenthesized.html)- `parsing`
- Parse a set of parentheses and expose their content to subsequent parsers.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_macro_input.html)- macro_ - input - `parsing`and- `proc-macro`
- Parse the input TokenStream of a macro, triggering a compile error if the tokens fail to parse.
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_quote.html)- quote - `parsing`and- `printing`
- Quasi-quotation macro that accepts input like the `quote!`
- [parse_](https://docs.rs/macro.parse_quote_spanned.html)- quote_ - spanned - `parsing`and- `printing`
- This macro is `parse_quote!``quote_spanned!`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Abi](https://docs.rs/struct.Abi.html)- `derive`or- `full`

- [Angle](https://docs.rs/struct.AngleBracketedGenericArguments.html)- Bracketed - Generic - Arguments - `derive`or- `full`

- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprMacro.html)- Macro - `derive`or- `full`
- A macro invocation expression: `format!("{}", q)`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprMatch.html)- Match - `full`
- A `match`expression:`match n { Some(n) => {}, None => {} }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprMethodCall.html)- Method - Call - `derive`or- `full`
- A method call expression: `x.foo::<T>(a, b)`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprParen.html)- Paren - `derive`or- `full`
- A parenthesized expression: `(a + b)`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprPath.html)- Path - `derive`or- `full`
- A path like `core::mem::replace`possibly containing generic parameters and a qualified self-type.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprRange.html)- Range - `full`
- A range expression: `1..2`,`1..`,`..2`,`1..=2`,`..=2`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprRawAddr.html)- RawAddr - `full`
- Address-of operation: `&raw const place`or`&raw mut place`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprReference.html)- Reference - `derive`or- `full`
- A referencing operation: `&a`or`&mut a`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprRepeat.html)- Repeat - `full`
- An array literal constructed from one repeated element: `[0u8; N]`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprReturn.html)- Return - `full`
- A `return`, with an optional value to be returned.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprStruct.html)- Struct - `derive`or- `full`
- A struct literal expression: `Point { x: 1, y: 1 }`.
- [ExprTry](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprTry.html)- `full`
- A try-expression: `expr?`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprTryBlock.html)- TryBlock - `full`
- A try block: `try { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprTuple.html)- Tuple - `full`
- A tuple expression: `(a, b, c, d)`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprUnary.html)- Unary - `derive`or- `full`
- A unary operation: `!x`,`*x`,`-x`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprUnsafe.html)- Unsafe - `full`
- An unsafe block: `unsafe { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprWhile.html)- While - `full`
- A while loop: `while expr { ... }`.
- [Expr](https://docs.rs/struct.ExprYield.html)- Yield - `full`
- A yield expression: `yield expr`.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.Field.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A field of a struct or enum variant.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldPat.html)- Pat - `full`
- A single field in a struct pattern.
- [Field](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldValue.html)- Value - `derive`or- `full`
- A field-value pair in a struct literal.
- [Fields](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldsNamed.html)- Named - `derive`or- `full`
- Named fields of a struct or struct variant such as `Point { x: f64, y: f64 }`.
- [Fields](https://docs.rs/struct.FieldsUnnamed.html)- Unnamed - `derive`or- `full`
- Unnamed fields of a tuple struct or tuple variant such as `Some(T)`.
- [File](https://docs.rs/struct.File.html)- `full`
- A complete file of Rust source code.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/struct.ForeignItemFn.html)- Item - Fn - `full`
- A foreign function in an `extern`block.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/struct.ForeignItemMacro.html)- Item - Macro - `full`
- A macro invocation within an extern block.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/struct.ForeignItemStatic.html)- Item - Static - `full`
- A foreign static item in an `extern`block:`static ext: u8`.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/struct.ForeignItemType.html)- Item - Type - `full`
- A foreign type in an `extern`block:`type void`.
- [Generics](https://docs.rs/struct.Generics.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- Lifetimes and type parameters attached to a declaration of a function, enum, trait, etc.
- [Ident](https://docs.rs/struct.Ident.html)
- A word of Rust code, which may be a keyword or legal variable name.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplGenerics.html)- Generics - `printing`and (- `derive`or- `full`)
- Returned by `Generics::split_for_impl`.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplItemConst.html)- Item - Const - `full`
- An associated constant within an impl block.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplItemFn.html)- Item - Fn - `full`
- An associated function within an impl block.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplItemMacro.html)- Item - Macro - `full`
- A macro invocation within an impl block.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/struct.ImplItemType.html)- Item - Type - `full`
- An associated type within an impl block.
- [Index](https://docs.rs/struct.Index.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- The index of an unnamed tuple struct field.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemConst.html)- Const - `full`
- A constant item: `const MAX: u16 = 65535`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemEnum.html)- Enum - `full`
- An enum definition: `enum Foo<A, B> { A(A), B(B) }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemExternCrate.html)- Extern - Crate - `full`
- An `extern crate`item:`extern crate serde`.
- [ItemFn](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemFn.html)- `full`
- A free-standing function: `fn process(n: usize) -> Result<()> { ... }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemForeignMod.html)- Foreign - Mod - `full`
- A block of foreign items: `extern "C" { ... }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemImpl.html)- Impl - `full`
- An impl block providing trait or associated items: `impl<A> Trait for Data<A> { ... }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemMacro.html)- Macro - `full`
- A macro invocation, which includes `macro_rules!`definitions.
- [ItemMod](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemMod.html)- `full`
- A module or module declaration: `mod m`or`mod m { ... }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemStatic.html)- Static - `full`
- A static item: `static BIKE: Shed = Shed(42)`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemStruct.html)- Struct - `full`
- A struct definition: `struct Foo<A> { x: A }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemTrait.html)- Trait - `full`
- A trait definition: `pub trait Iterator { ... }`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemTraitAlias.html)- Trait - Alias - `full`
- A trait alias: `pub trait SharableIterator = Iterator + Sync`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemType.html)- Type - `full`
- A type alias: `type Result<T> = core::result::Result<T, MyError>`.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemUnion.html)- Union - `full`
- A union definition: `union Foo<A, B> { x: A, y: B }`.
- [ItemUse](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemUse.html)- `full`
- A use declaration: `use alloc::collections::HashMap`.
- [Label](https://docs.rs/struct.Label.html)- `full`
- A lifetime labeling a `for`,`while`, or`loop`.
- [Lifetime](https://docs.rs/struct.Lifetime.html)
- A Rust lifetime: `'a`.
- [Lifetime](https://docs.rs/struct.LifetimeParam.html)- Param - `derive`or- `full`
- A lifetime definition: `'a: 'b + 'c + 'd`.
- [LitBool](https://docs.rs/struct.LitBool.html)
- A boolean literal: `true`or`false`.
- [LitByte](https://docs.rs/struct.LitByte.html)
- A byte literal: `b'f'`.
- [LitByte](https://docs.rs/struct.LitByteStr.html)- Str
- A byte string literal: `b"foo"`.

- A nul-terminated C-string literal: `c"foo"`.
- [LitChar](https://docs.rs/struct.LitChar.html)
- A character literal: `'a'`.
- [LitFloat](https://docs.rs/struct.LitFloat.html)
- A floating point literal: `1f64`or`1.0e10f64`.
- [LitInt](https://docs.rs/struct.LitInt.html)
- An integer literal: `1`or`1u16`.
- [LitStr](https://docs.rs/struct.LitStr.html)
- A UTF-8 string literal: `"foo"`.
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.Local.html)- `full`
- A local `let`binding:`let x: u64 = s.parse()?;`.

- [Parenthesized](https://docs.rs/struct.ParenthesizedGenericArguments.html)- Generic - Arguments - `derive`or- `full`

- [PatIdent](https://docs.rs/struct.PatIdent.html)- `full`

- [PatLit](https://docs.rs/struct.PatLit.html)- `full`

- [PatSlice](https://docs.rs/struct.PatSlice.html)- `full`

- [Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Path.html)- `derive`or- `full`

- A macro in the type position.

- The never type: `!`.

- A generic type parameter: `T: Into<String>`.

- A parenthesized type equivalent to the inner type.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypePath.html)- Path - `derive`or- `full`
- A path like `core::slice::Iter`, optionally qualified with a self-type as in`<Vec<T> as SomeTrait>::Associated`.
- [TypePtr](https://docs.rs/struct.TypePtr.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A raw pointer type: `*const T`or`*mut T`.

- A reference type: `&'a T`or`&'a mut T`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeSlice.html)- Slice - `derive`or- `full`
- A dynamically sized slice type: `[T]`.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/struct.TypeTraitObject.html)- Trait - Object - `derive`or- `full`
- A trait object type `dyn Bound1 + Bound2 + Bound3`where`Bound`is a trait or a lifetime.

- A glob import in a `use`item:`*`.
- [UseGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.UseGroup.html)- `full`
- A braced group of imports in a `use`item:`{A, B, C}`.

- An identifier imported by a `use`item:`HashMap`.
- [UsePath](https://docs.rs/struct.UsePath.html)- `full`

- [UseRename](https://docs.rs/struct.UseRename.html)- `full`

- A `where`clause in a definition:`where T: Deserialize<'de>, D: 'static`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Attr](https://docs.rs/enum.AttrStyle.html)- Style - `derive`or- `full`
- Distinguishes between attributes that decorate an item and attributes that are contained within an item.
- [BinOp](https://docs.rs/enum.BinOp.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A binary operator: `+`,`+=`,`&`.

- Single parameter in a precise capturing bound.

- Unused, but reserved for RFC 3323 restrictions.

- Data stored within an enum variant or struct.
- [FnArg](https://docs.rs/enum.FnArg.html)- `full`
- An argument in a function signature: the `n: usize`in`fn f(n: usize)`.
- [Foreign](https://docs.rs/enum.ForeignItem.html)- Item - `full`
- An item within an `extern`block.
- [Generic](https://docs.rs/enum.GenericArgument.html)- Argument - `derive`or- `full`
- An individual generic argument, like `'a`,`T`, or`Item = T`.
- [Generic](https://docs.rs/enum.GenericParam.html)- Param - `derive`or- `full`
- A generic type parameter, lifetime, or const generic: `T: Into<String>`,`'a: 'b`,`const LEN: usize`.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/enum.ImplItem.html)- Item - `full`
- An item within an impl block.
- [Impl](https://docs.rs/enum.ImplRestriction.html)- Restriction - `full`
- Unused, but reserved for RFC 3323 restrictions.
- [Item](https://docs.rs/enum.Item.html)- `full`
- Things that can appear directly inside of a module or scope.
- [Lit](https://docs.rs/enum.Lit.html)
- A Rust literal such as a string or integer or boolean.
- [Macro](https://docs.rs/enum.MacroDelimiter.html)- Delimiter - `derive`or- `full`
- A grouping token that surrounds a macro body: `m!(...)`or`m!{...}`or`m![...]`.
- [Member](https://docs.rs/enum.Member.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A struct or tuple struct field accessed in a struct literal or field expression.
- [Meta](https://docs.rs/enum.Meta.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- Content of a compile-time structured attribute.
- [Pat](https://docs.rs/enum.Pat.html)- `full`
- A pattern in a local binding, function signature, match expression, or various other places.
- [Path](https://docs.rs/enum.PathArguments.html)- Arguments - `derive`or- `full`
- Angle bracketed or parenthesized arguments of a path segment.
- [Pointer](https://docs.rs/enum.PointerMutability.html)- Mutability - `full`
- Mutability of a raw pointer (`*const T`,`*mut T`), in which non-mutable isn’t the implicit default.
- [Range](https://docs.rs/enum.RangeLimits.html)- Limits - `full`
- Limit types of a range, inclusive or exclusive.
- [Return](https://docs.rs/enum.ReturnType.html)- Type - `derive`or- `full`
- Return type of a function signature.
- [Static](https://docs.rs/enum.StaticMutability.html)- Mutability - `full`
- The mutability of an `Item::Static`or`ForeignItem::Static`.
- [Stmt](https://docs.rs/enum.Stmt.html)- `full`
- A statement, usually ending in a semicolon.
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/enum.TraitBoundModifier.html)- Bound - Modifier - `derive`or- `full`
- A modifier on a trait bound, currently only used for the `?`in`?Sized`.
- [Trait](https://docs.rs/enum.TraitItem.html)- Item - `full`
- An item declaration within the definition of a trait.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/enum.Type.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- The possible types that a Rust value could have.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/enum.TypeParamBound.html)- Param - Bound - `derive`or- `full`
- A trait or lifetime used as a bound on a type parameter.
- [UnOp](https://docs.rs/enum.UnOp.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- A unary operator: `*`,`!`,`-`.
- [UseTree](https://docs.rs/enum.UseTree.html)- `full`
- A suffix of an import tree in a `use`item:`Type as Renamed`or`*`.
- [Visibility](https://docs.rs/enum.Visibility.html)- `derive`or- `full`
- The visibility level of an item: inherited or `pub`or`pub(restricted)`.
- [Where](https://docs.rs/enum.WherePredicate.html)- Predicate - `derive`or- `full`
- A single predicate in a `where`clause:`T: Deserialize<'de>`.

# rship_entities_macros/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Proc macros for rship entities
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! Provides the `#[binding_node]` attribute macro for defining binding nodes.
[4](https://docs.rs#4)
[5](https://docs.rs#5)use convert_case::{Case, Casing};
[6](https://docs.rs#6)use proc_macro::TokenStream;
[7](https://docs.rs#7)use quote::quote;
[8](https://docs.rs#8)use syn::{ItemStruct, parse_macro_input};
[9](https://docs.rs#9)
[10](https://docs.rs#10)/// Attribute macro for defining a binding node
[11](https://docs.rs#11)///
[12](https://docs.rs#12)/// This macro is applied to a struct definition and generates:
[13](https://docs.rs#13)/// - The struct itself with associated constants (TYPE_ID, NAME, CATEGORY)
[14](https://docs.rs#14)/// - Inventory registration for runtime discovery
[15](https://docs.rs#15)///
[16](https://docs.rs#16)/// After applying this macro, you must implement:
[17](https://docs.rs#17)/// - `StaticAnchors` (for static nodes) or `ReactiveAnchors` (for dynamic nodes)
[18](https://docs.rs#18)/// - Either `PureNode` (for synchronous compute) or `CellNode` (for reactive cells)
[19](https://docs.rs#19)///
[20](https://docs.rs#20)/// # Example - Pure Node (static anchors)
[21](https://docs.rs#21)///
[22](https://docs.rs#22)/// ```ignore
[23](https://docs.rs#23)/// use crate::binding_node_executor::{StaticAnchors, PureNode, SchemaToken, AnchorDef, anchor};
[24](https://docs.rs#24)///
[25](https://docs.rs#25)/// #[binding_node(category = crate::LOGIC, pure)]
[26](https://docs.rs#26)/// pub struct GateNode;
[27](https://docs.rs#27)///
[28](https://docs.rs#28)/// impl StaticAnchors for GateNode {
[29](https://docs.rs#29)///     fn input_anchors() -> Vec<AnchorDef> {
[30](https://docs.rs#30)///         vec![anchor("value", SchemaToken::T), anchor("open", SchemaToken::BOOL)]
[31](https://docs.rs#31)///     }
[32](https://docs.rs#32)///
[33](https://docs.rs#33)///     fn output_anchors() -> Vec<AnchorDef> {
[34](https://docs.rs#34)///         vec![anchor("output", SchemaToken::T)]
[35](https://docs.rs#35)///     }
[36](https://docs.rs#36)/// }
[37](https://docs.rs#37)///
[38](https://docs.rs#38)/// impl PureNode for GateNode {
[39](https://docs.rs#39)///     fn compute(get_input: &dyn Fn(&str) -> BindingValue, _output_id: &str) -> BindingValue {
[40](https://docs.rs#40)///         let open = get_input("open").to_bool();
[41](https://docs.rs#41)///         if open { get_input("value") } else { BindingValue::Null }
[42](https://docs.rs#42)///     }
[43](https://docs.rs#43)/// }
[44](https://docs.rs#44)/// ```
[45](https://docs.rs#45)///
[46](https://docs.rs#46)/// # Example - Cell Node (static anchors)
[47](https://docs.rs#47)///
[48](https://docs.rs#48)/// ```ignore
[49](https://docs.rs#49)/// use hyphae::{Cell, CellImmutable, SampleExt, Pipeline, MaterializeDefinite};
[50](https://docs.rs#50)///
[51](https://docs.rs#51)/// #[binding_node(category = crate::LOGIC, cell)]
[52](https://docs.rs#52)/// pub struct SampleNode;
[53](https://docs.rs#53)///
[54](https://docs.rs#54)/// impl StaticAnchors for SampleNode {
[55](https://docs.rs#55)///     fn input_anchors() -> Vec<AnchorDef> {
[56](https://docs.rs#56)///         vec![anchor("trigger", SchemaToken::ANY), anchor("emitter", SchemaToken::T)]
[57](https://docs.rs#57)///     }
[58](https://docs.rs#58)///
[59](https://docs.rs#59)///     fn output_anchors() -> Vec<AnchorDef> {
[60](https://docs.rs#60)///         vec![anchor("output", SchemaToken::T)]
[61](https://docs.rs#61)///     }
[62](https://docs.rs#62)/// }
[63](https://docs.rs#63)///
[64](https://docs.rs#64)/// impl CellNode for SampleNode {
[65](https://docs.rs#65)///     fn make_cell(ctx: NodeExecutionContext) -> impl MaterializeDefinite<BindingDatagram> {
[66](https://docs.rs#66)///         let trigger = ctx.input_cell("trigger");
[67](https://docs.rs#67)///         let emitter = ctx.input_cell("emitter");
[68](https://docs.rs#68)///         emitter.sample(&trigger)
[69](https://docs.rs#69)///     }
[70](https://docs.rs#70)/// }
[71](https://docs.rs#71)/// ```
[72](https://docs.rs#72)#[proc_macro_attribute]
[73](https://docs.rs#73)pub fn binding_node(attr: TokenStream, item: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
[74](https://docs.rs#74)    let args = parse_macro_input!(attr as BindingNodeArgs);
[75](https://docs.rs#75)    let input = parse_macro_input!(item as ItemStruct);
[76](https://docs.rs#76)
[77](https://docs.rs#77)    match generate_binding_node(args, input) {
[78](https://docs.rs#78)        Ok(tokens) => tokens.into(),
[79](https://docs.rs#79)        Err(e) => e.to_compile_error().into(),
[80](https://docs.rs#80)    }
[81](https://docs.rs#81)}
[82](https://docs.rs#82)
[83](https://docs.rs#83)/// Executor mode for a binding node
[84](https://docs.rs#84)#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
[85](https://docs.rs#85)enum ExecutorMode {
[86](https://docs.rs#86)    /// Pure node (uses PureNode trait)
[87](https://docs.rs#87)    Pure,
[88](https://docs.rs#88)    /// Cell-based node (uses CellNode trait)
[89](https://docs.rs#89)    Cell,
[90](https://docs.rs#90)}
[91](https://docs.rs#91)
[92](https://docs.rs#92)/// Arguments to `#[binding_node(...)]`
[93](https://docs.rs#93)struct BindingNodeArgs {
[94](https://docs.rs#94)    /// Category expression — a const path (e.g. `crate::MATH`) or string literal.
[95](https://docs.rs#95)    /// Const paths are preferred for compile-time verification.
[96](https://docs.rs#96)    category: syn::Expr,
[97](https://docs.rs#97)    /// The executor mode for this node
[98](https://docs.rs#98)    executor_mode: ExecutorMode,
[99](https://docs.rs#99)    /// Whether this node should be hidden from the palette/sidebar
[100](https://docs.rs#100)    hidden: bool,
[101](https://docs.rs#101)}
[102](https://docs.rs#102)
[103](https://docs.rs#103)impl syn::parse::Parse for BindingNodeArgs {
[104](https://docs.rs#104)    fn parse(input: syn::parse::ParseStream) -> syn::Result<Self> {
[105](https://docs.rs#105)        use syn::Token;
[106](https://docs.rs#106)
[107](https://docs.rs#107)        let mut category = None;
[108](https://docs.rs#108)        let mut pure = false;
[109](https://docs.rs#109)        let mut cell = false;
[110](https://docs.rs#110)        let mut hidden = false;
[111](https://docs.rs#111)
[112](https://docs.rs#112)        while !input.is_empty() {
[113](https://docs.rs#113)            let key: syn::Ident = input.parse()?;
[114](https://docs.rs#114)            match key.to_string().as_str() {
[115](https://docs.rs#115)                "category" => {
[116](https://docs.rs#116)                    input.parse::<Token![=]>()?;
[117](https://docs.rs#117)                    category = Some(input.parse::<syn::Expr>()?);
[118](https://docs.rs#118)                }
[119](https://docs.rs#119)                "pure" => {
[120](https://docs.rs#120)                    pure = true;
[121](https://docs.rs#121)                }
[122](https://docs.rs#122)                "cell" => {
[123](https://docs.rs#123)                    cell = true;
[124](https://docs.rs#124)                }
[125](https://docs.rs#125)                "hidden" => {
[126](https://docs.rs#126)                    hidden = true;
[127](https://docs.rs#127)                }
[128](https://docs.rs#128)                _ => {
[129](https://docs.rs#129)                    return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(
[130](https://docs.rs#130)                        key,
[131](https://docs.rs#131)                        "Expected: category, pure, cell, or hidden",
[132](https://docs.rs#132)                    ));
[133](https://docs.rs#133)                }
[134](https://docs.rs#134)            }
[135](https://docs.rs#135)
[136](https://docs.rs#136)            // Optional trailing comma
[137](https://docs.rs#137)            let _ = input.parse::<Token![,]>();
[138](https://docs.rs#138)        }
[139](https://docs.rs#139)
[140](https://docs.rs#140)        let category = category.ok_or_else(|| input.error("Missing required: category = ..."))?;
[141](https://docs.rs#141)
[142](https://docs.rs#142)        // Validate that exactly one of pure/cell is specified
[143](https://docs.rs#143)        if pure && cell {
[144](https://docs.rs#144)            return Err(input.error("Cannot specify both 'pure' and 'cell'"));
[145](https://docs.rs#145)        }
[146](https://docs.rs#146)        if !pure && !cell {
[147](https://docs.rs#147)            return Err(input.error("Must specify either 'pure' or 'cell'"));
[148](https://docs.rs#148)        }
[149](https://docs.rs#149)
[150](https://docs.rs#150)        let executor_mode = if pure {
[151](https://docs.rs#151)            ExecutorMode::Pure
[152](https://docs.rs#152)        } else {
[153](https://docs.rs#153)            ExecutorMode::Cell
[154](https://docs.rs#154)        };
[155](https://docs.rs#155)
[156](https://docs.rs#156)        Ok(BindingNodeArgs {
[157](https://docs.rs#157)            category,
[158](https://docs.rs#158)            executor_mode,
[159](https://docs.rs#159)            hidden,
[160](https://docs.rs#160)        })
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    }
[162](https://docs.rs#162)}
[163](https://docs.rs#163)
[164](https://docs.rs#164)fn generate_binding_node(
[165](https://docs.rs#165)    args: BindingNodeArgs,
[166](https://docs.rs#166)    input: ItemStruct,
[167](https://docs.rs#167)) -> syn::Result<proc_macro2::TokenStream> {
[168](https://docs.rs#168)    let node_struct_name = &input.ident;
[169](https://docs.rs#169)    let vis = &input.vis;
[170](https://docs.rs#170)    let attrs = &input.attrs;
[171](https://docs.rs#171)
[172](https://docs.rs#172)    // Derive the node name from the struct name (remove "Node" suffix if present)
[173](https://docs.rs#173)    let struct_name_str = node_struct_name.to_string();
[174](https://docs.rs#174)    let node_name = if struct_name_str.ends_with("Node") {
[175](https://docs.rs#175)        struct_name_str.strip_suffix("Node").unwrap().to_string()
[176](https://docs.rs#176)    } else {
[177](https://docs.rs#177)        struct_name_str.clone()
[178](https://docs.rs#178)    };
[179](https://docs.rs#179)
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    // Convert PascalCase to kebab-case for type_id
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    let type_id = node_name.to_case(Case::Kebab);
[182](https://docs.rs#182)    let display_name = node_name.to_case(Case::Title);
[183](https://docs.rs#183)    let camel_case_name = node_name.to_case(Case::Camel);
[184](https://docs.rs#184)
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    let category = &args.category;
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    let hidden = args.hidden;
[187](https://docs.rs#187)
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    // Generate the executor registration based on executor mode.
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    //
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    // For Cell nodes the trait methods now return `impl Pipeline<...>`, so we
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    // wrap them in module-position `fn` items that materialize at the
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    // registration boundary. The wrapper has a concrete `Cell<...>` return
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    // type that matches the function-pointer slot in `NodeRegistration`.
[194](https://docs.rs#194)    let executor_registration = match args.executor_mode {
[195](https://docs.rs#195)        ExecutorMode::Pure => {
[196](https://docs.rs#196)            quote! {
[197](https://docs.rs#197)                ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::NodeExecutor::Pure(
[198](https://docs.rs#198)                    <#node_struct_name as ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::PureNode>::compute
[199](https://docs.rs#199)                )
[200](https://docs.rs#200)            }
[201](https://docs.rs#201)        }
[202](https://docs.rs#202)        ExecutorMode::Cell => {
[203](https://docs.rs#203)            quote! {
[204](https://docs.rs#204)                ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::NodeExecutor::Cell {
[205](https://docs.rs#205)                    make_cell: {
[206](https://docs.rs#206)                        fn __make_cell(
[207](https://docs.rs#207)                            ctx: ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::NodeExecutionContext,
[208](https://docs.rs#208)                        ) -> ::hyphae::Cell<
[209](https://docs.rs#209)                            ::rship_entities_foundation::BindingDatagram,
[210](https://docs.rs#210)                            ::hyphae::CellImmutable,
[211](https://docs.rs#211)                        > {
[212](https://docs.rs#212)                            use ::hyphae::MaterializeDefinite;
[213](https://docs.rs#213)                            <#node_struct_name as ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::CellNode>::make_cell(ctx).materialize()
[214](https://docs.rs#214)                        }
[215](https://docs.rs#215)                        __make_cell
[216](https://docs.rs#216)                    },
[217](https://docs.rs#217)                    make_exec_cell: {
[218](https://docs.rs#218)                        fn __make_exec_cell(
[219](https://docs.rs#219)                            ctx: ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::NodeExecutionContext,
[220](https://docs.rs#220)                        ) -> ::hyphae::Cell<
[221](https://docs.rs#221)                            ::rship_entities_foundation::ExecDatagram,
[222](https://docs.rs#222)                            ::hyphae::CellImmutable,
[223](https://docs.rs#223)                        > {
[224](https://docs.rs#224)                            use ::hyphae::MaterializeDefinite;
[225](https://docs.rs#225)                            <#node_struct_name as ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::CellNode>::make_exec_cell(ctx).materialize()
[226](https://docs.rs#226)                        }
[227](https://docs.rs#227)                        __make_exec_cell
[228](https://docs.rs#228)                    },
[229](https://docs.rs#229)                }
[230](https://docs.rs#230)            }
[231](https://docs.rs#231)        }
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    };
[233](https://docs.rs#233)
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    // Generate the output
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    let expanded = quote! {
[236](https://docs.rs#236)        #(#attrs)*
[237](https://docs.rs#237)        #vis struct #node_struct_name;
[238](https://docs.rs#238)
[239](https://docs.rs#239)        impl #node_struct_name {
[240](https://docs.rs#240)            /// The raw node name (PascalCase, without "Node" suffix)
[241](https://docs.rs#241)            pub const NAME: &'static str = #node_name;
[242](https://docs.rs#242)
[243](https://docs.rs#243)            /// The node type ID (kebab-case)
[244](https://docs.rs#244)            pub const TYPE_ID: &'static str = #type_id;
[245](https://docs.rs#245)
[246](https://docs.rs#246)            /// Display name for UI
[247](https://docs.rs#247)            pub const DISPLAY_NAME: &'static str = #display_name;
[248](https://docs.rs#248)
[249](https://docs.rs#249)            /// camelCase name
[250](https://docs.rs#250)            pub const CAMEL_CASE_NAME: &'static str = #camel_case_name;
[251](https://docs.rs#251)
[252](https://docs.rs#252)            /// Node category (kebab-case ID)
[253](https://docs.rs#253)            pub const CATEGORY: &'static str = #category;
[254](https://docs.rs#254)
[255](https://docs.rs#255)            /// Get the complete node definition.
[256](https://docs.rs#256)            ///
[257](https://docs.rs#257)            /// This looks up the registered node definition from the inventory.
[258](https://docs.rs#258)            pub fn def() -> ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::NodeDef {
[259](https://docs.rs#259)                ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::node_def::find_node_def(Self::TYPE_ID)
[260](https://docs.rs#260)                    .expect("Node should be registered")
[261](https://docs.rs#261)            }
[262](https://docs.rs#262)        }
[263](https://docs.rs#263)
[264](https://docs.rs#264)        // Register with inventory for typegen and execution.
[265](https://docs.rs#265)        //
[266](https://docs.rs#266)        // ReactiveAnchors methods now return `impl Pipeline<...>`. The
[267](https://docs.rs#267)        // function-pointer slots in `NodeRegistration` still expect concrete
[268](https://docs.rs#268)        // `fn(...) -> Cell<...>`, so we wrap each trait call in a module
[269](https://docs.rs#269)        // `fn` that materializes at the registration boundary.
[270](https://docs.rs#270)        ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::inventory::submit! {
[271](https://docs.rs#271)            ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::NodeRegistration {
[272](https://docs.rs#272)                type_id: #type_id,
[273](https://docs.rs#273)                display_name: #display_name,
[274](https://docs.rs#274)                category: #category,
[275](https://docs.rs#275)                hidden_from_palette: #hidden,
[276](https://docs.rs#276)                input_anchors_cell: {
[277](https://docs.rs#277)                    fn __input_anchors_cell(
[278](https://docs.rs#278)                        ctx: &::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::SchemaResolutionContext,
[279](https://docs.rs#279)                    ) -> ::hyphae::Cell<
[280](https://docs.rs#280)                        ::std::vec::Vec<::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::LabeledAnchorDef>,
[281](https://docs.rs#281)                        ::hyphae::CellImmutable,
[282](https://docs.rs#282)                    > {
[283](https://docs.rs#283)                        use ::hyphae::MaterializeDefinite;
[284](https://docs.rs#284)                        <#node_struct_name as ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::ReactiveAnchors>::input_anchors_cell(ctx).materialize()
[285](https://docs.rs#285)                    }
[286](https://docs.rs#286)                    __input_anchors_cell
[287](https://docs.rs#287)                },
[288](https://docs.rs#288)                output_anchors_cell: {
[289](https://docs.rs#289)                    fn __output_anchors_cell(
[290](https://docs.rs#290)                        ctx: &::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::SchemaResolutionContext,
[291](https://docs.rs#291)                    ) -> ::hyphae::Cell<
[292](https://docs.rs#292)                        ::std::vec::Vec<::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::LabeledAnchorDef>,
[293](https://docs.rs#293)                        ::hyphae::CellImmutable,
[294](https://docs.rs#294)                    > {
[295](https://docs.rs#295)                        use ::hyphae::MaterializeDefinite;
[296](https://docs.rs#296)                        <#node_struct_name as ::rship_entities_nodes::binding_node_executor::ReactiveAnchors>::output_anchors_cell(ctx).materialize()
[297](https://docs.rs#297)                    }

[299](https://docs.rs#299)                },

# binding_node in rship_entities_macros - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-entities-macros/4.0.0-canary.63/rship_entities_macros/attr.binding_node.html

`#[binding_node]`## Expand description

Attribute macro for defining a binding node

This macro is applied to a struct definition and generates:

- The struct itself with associated constants (TYPE_ID, NAME, CATEGORY)
- Inventory registration for runtime discovery

After applying this macro, you must implement:

- `StaticAnchors`(for static nodes) or- `ReactiveAnchors`(for dynamic nodes)
- Either `PureNode`(for synchronous compute) or`CellNode`(for reactive cells)

[§](https://docs.rs#example---pure-node-static-anchors)Example - Pure Node (static anchors)

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use crate::binding_node_executor::{StaticAnchors, PureNode, SchemaToken, AnchorDef, anchor};
#[binding_node(category = crate::LOGIC, pure)]
pub struct GateNode;
impl StaticAnchors for GateNode {
    fn input_anchors() -> Vec<AnchorDef> {
        vec![anchor("value", SchemaToken::T), anchor("open", SchemaToken::BOOL)]
    }
    fn output_anchors() -> Vec<AnchorDef> {
        vec![anchor("output", SchemaToken::T)]
    }
}
impl PureNode for GateNode {
    fn compute(get_input: &dyn Fn(&str) -> BindingValue, _output_id: &str) -> BindingValue {
        let open = get_input("open").to_bool();
        if open { get_input("value") } else { BindingValue::Null }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#example---cell-node-static-anchors)Example - Cell Node (static anchors)

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use hyphae::{Cell, CellImmutable, SampleExt, Pipeline, MaterializeDefinite};
#[binding_node(category = crate::LOGIC, cell)]
pub struct SampleNode;
impl StaticAnchors for SampleNode {
    fn input_anchors() -> Vec<AnchorDef> {
        vec![anchor("trigger", SchemaToken::ANY), anchor("emitter", SchemaToken::T)]
    }
    fn output_anchors() -> Vec<AnchorDef> {
        vec![anchor("output", SchemaToken::T)]
    }
}
impl CellNode for SampleNode {
    fn make_cell(ctx: NodeExecutionContext) -> impl MaterializeDefinite<BindingDatagram> {
        let trigger = ctx.input_cell("trigger");
        let emitter = ctx.input_cell("emitter");
        emitter.sample(&trigger)
    }
}
```

# anyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/anyhow/^1.0.102/

## Expand description

This library provides [ anyhow::Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html), a trait object based error
type for easy idiomatic error handling in Rust applications.

[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Use `Result<T, anyhow::Error>`, or equivalently`anyhow::Result<T>`, as the return type of any fallible function.Within the function, use `?`to easily propagate any error that implements the`std::error::Error``use anyhow::Result; fn get_cluster_info() -> Result<ClusterMap> { let config = std::fs::read_to_string("cluster.json")?; let map: ClusterMap = serde_json::from_str(&config)?; Ok(map) }`
-
Attach context to help the person troubleshooting the error understand where things went wrong. A low-level error like “No such file or directory” can be annoying to debug without more context about what higher level step the application was in the middle of. `use anyhow::{Context, Result}; fn main() -> Result<()> { ... it.detach().context("Failed to detach the important thing")?; let content = std::fs::read(path) .with_context(|| format!("Failed to read instrs from {}", path))?; ... }``Error: Failed to read instrs from ./path/to/instrs.json Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)`
-
Downcasting is supported and can be by value, by shared reference, or by mutable reference as needed. `// If the error was caused by redaction, then return a // tombstone instead of the content. match root_cause.downcast_ref::<DataStoreError>() { Some(DataStoreError::Censored(_)) => Ok(Poll::Ready(REDACTED_CONTENT)), None => Err(error), }`
-
If using Rust ≥ 1.65, a backtrace is captured and printed with the error if the underlying error type does not already provide its own. In order to see backtraces, they must be enabled through the environment variables described in `std::backtrace`- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only errors to have backtraces, set `RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only panics to have backtraces, set `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`and`RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=0`.

- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
-
Anyhow works with any error type that has an impl of `std::error::Error`, including ones defined in your crate. We do not bundle a`derive(Error)`macro but you can write the impls yourself or use a standalone macro like[thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror).`use thiserror::Error; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum FormatError { #[error("Invalid header (expected {expected:?}, got {found:?})")] InvalidHeader { expected: String, found: String, }, #[error("Missing attribute: {0}")] MissingAttribute(String), }`
-
One-off error messages can be constructed using the `anyhow!`macro, which supports string interpolation and produces an`anyhow::Error`.`return Err(anyhow!("Missing attribute: {}", missing));`A `bail!`macro is provided as a shorthand for the same early return.`bail!("Missing attribute: {}", missing);`

[§](https://docs.rs#no-std-support)No-std support

In no_std mode, almost all of the same API is available and works the same way. To depend on Anyhow in no_std mode, disable our default enabled “std” feature in Cargo.toml. A global allocator is required.

```
[dependencies]
anyhow = { version = "1.0", default-features = false }
```
With versions of Rust older than 1.81, no_std mode may require an additional
`.map_err(Error::msg)` when working with a non-Anyhow error type inside a
function that returns Anyhow’s error type, as the trait that `?`-based error
conversions are defined by is only available in std in those old versions.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [anyhow](https://docs.rs/macro.anyhow.html)as format_err;

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [anyhow](https://docs.rs/macro.anyhow.html)
- Construct an ad-hoc error from a string or existing non-`anyhow`error value.
- [bail](https://docs.rs/macro.bail.html)
- Return early with an error.
- [ensure](https://docs.rs/macro.ensure.html)
- Return early with an error if a condition is not satisfied.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- Iterator of a chain of source errors.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- The `Error`type, a wrapper around a dynamic error type.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Context](https://docs.rs/trait.Context.html)
- Provides the `context`method for`Result`.

- Equivalent to `Ok::<_, anyhow::Error>(value)`.

# jsonrpc_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/jsonrpc-core/^18.0.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#transport-agnostic-jsonrpc-library)Transport agnostic jsonrpc library.

Right now it supports only server side handling requests.

```
use jsonrpc_core::IoHandler;
use jsonrpc_core::Value;
let mut io = IoHandler::new();
io.add_sync_method("say_hello", |_| {
    Ok(Value::String("Hello World!".into()))
});
let request = r#"{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "say_hello", "params": [42, 23], "id": 1}"#;
let response = r#"{"jsonrpc":"2.0","result":"Hello World!","id":1}"#;
assert_eq!(io.handle_request_sync(request), Some(response.to_string()));
```

# reqwest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reqwest/^0.12.28/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#reqwest)reqwest

The `reqwest` crate provides a convenient, higher-level HTTP
[ Client](https://docs.rs/struct.Client.html).

It handles many of the things that most people just expect an HTTP client to do for them.

- Async and [blocking](https://docs.rs/blocking/index.html)Clients
- Plain bodies, [JSON](https://docs.rs#json),[urlencoded](https://docs.rs#forms),[multipart](https://docs.rs/multipart/index.html)
- Customizable [redirect policy](https://docs.rs#redirect-policies)
- HTTP [Proxies](https://docs.rs#proxies)
- Uses [TLS](https://docs.rs#tls)by default
- Cookies

The [ reqwest::Client](https://docs.rs/struct.Client.html) is asynchronous (requiring Tokio). For
applications wishing  to only make a few HTTP requests, the

[API may be more convenient.](https://docs.rs/blocking/index.html)

`reqwest::blocking`Additional learning resources include:

[§](https://docs.rs#commercial-support)Commercial Support

For private advice, support, reviews, access to the maintainer, and the
like, reach out for [commercial support](https://seanmonstar.com/sponsor).

[§](https://docs.rs#making-a-get-request)Making a GET request

For a single request, you can use the [ get](https://docs.rs/fn.get.html) shortcut method.

```
let body = reqwest::get("https://www.rust-lang.org")
    .await?
    .text()
    .await?;
println!("body = {body:?}");
```
**NOTE**: If you plan to perform multiple requests, it is best to create a
[ Client](https://docs.rs/struct.Client.html) and reuse it, taking advantage of keep-alive connection
pooling.

[§](https://docs.rs#making-post-requests-or-setting-request-bodies)Making POST requests (or setting request bodies)

There are several ways you can set the body of a request. The basic one is
by using the `body()` method of a [ RequestBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.RequestBuilder.html). This lets you set the
exact raw bytes of what the body should be. It accepts various types,
including

`String` and `Vec<u8>`. If you wish to pass a custom
type, you can use the `reqwest::Body` constructors.```
let client = reqwest::Client::new();
let res = client.post("http://httpbin.org/post")
    .body("the exact body that is sent")
    .send()
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#forms)Forms

It’s very common to want to send form data in a request body. This can be done with any type that can be serialized into form data.

This can be an array of tuples, or a `HashMap`, or a custom type that
implements [ Serialize](http://serde.rs).

```
// This will POST a body of `foo=bar&baz=quux`
let params = [("foo", "bar"), ("baz", "quux")];
let client = reqwest::Client::new();
let res = client.post("http://httpbin.org/post")
    .form(¶ms)
    .send()
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#json)JSON

There is also a `json` method helper on the [ RequestBuilder](https://docs.rs/struct.RequestBuilder.html) that works in
a similar fashion the

`form` method. It can take any value that can be
serialized into JSON. The feature `json` is required.```
// This will POST a body of `{"lang":"rust","body":"json"}`
let mut map = HashMap::new();
map.insert("lang", "rust");
map.insert("body", "json");
let client = reqwest::Client::new();
let res = client.post("http://httpbin.org/post")
    .json(&map)
    .send()
    .await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#redirect-policies)Redirect Policies

By default, a `Client` will automatically handle HTTP redirects, having a
maximum redirect chain of 10 hops. To customize this behavior, a
[ redirect::Policy](https://docs.rs/redirect/index.html) can be used with a

`ClientBuilder`.[§](https://docs.rs#cookies)Cookies

The automatic storing and sending of session cookies can be enabled with
the [ cookie_store](https://docs.rs/struct.ClientBuilder.html#method.cookie_store) method on

`ClientBuilder`.[§](https://docs.rs#proxies)Proxies

**NOTE**: System proxies are enabled by default.

System proxies look in environment variables to set HTTP or HTTPS proxies.

`HTTP_PROXY` or `http_proxy` provide HTTP proxies for HTTP connections while
`HTTPS_PROXY` or `https_proxy` provide HTTPS proxies for HTTPS connections.
`ALL_PROXY` or `all_proxy` provide proxies for both HTTP and HTTPS connections.
If both the all proxy and HTTP or HTTPS proxy variables are set the more specific
HTTP or HTTPS proxies take precedence.

These can be overwritten by adding a [ Proxy](https://docs.rs/struct.Proxy.html) to

`ClientBuilder`
i.e. `let proxy = reqwest::Proxy::http("https://secure.example")?;`
or disabled by calling `ClientBuilder::no_proxy()`.`socks` feature is required if you have configured socks proxy like this:

`export https_proxy=socks5://127.0.0.1:1086`[§](https://docs.rs#tls)TLS

A `Client` will use transport layer security (TLS) by default to connect to
HTTPS destinations.

- Additional server certificates can be configured on a `ClientBuilder`with the`Certificate`
- Client certificates can be added to a `ClientBuilder`with the`Identity`
- Various parts of TLS can also be configured or even disabled on the
`ClientBuilder`.

See more details in the [ tls](https://docs.rs/tls/index.html) module.

[§](https://docs.rs#wasm)WASM

The Client implementation automatically switches to the WASM one when the target_arch is wasm32,
the usage is basically the same as the async api. Some of the features are disabled in wasm
: [ tls](https://docs.rs/tls/index.html),

[,](https://docs.rs/cookie/index.html)

`cookie`[, as well as various](https://docs.rs/blocking/index.html)

`blocking``ClientBuilder` methods such as `timeout()` and `connector_layer()`.TLS and cookies are provided through the browser environment, so reqwest can issue TLS requests with cookies, but has limited configuration.

[§](https://docs.rs#optional-features)Optional Features

The following are a list of [Cargo features](https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-features-section) that can be
enabled or disabled:

- **http2**- *(enabled by default)*: Enables HTTP/2 support.
- **default-tls**- *(enabled by default)*: Provides TLS support to connect over HTTPS.
- **native-tls**: Enables TLS functionality provided by- `native-tls`.
- **native-tls-vendored**: Enables the- `vendored`feature of- `native-tls`.
- **native-tls-alpn**: Enables the- `alpn`feature of- `native-tls`.
- **rustls-tls**: Enables TLS functionality provided by- `rustls`. Equivalent to- `rustls-tls-webpki-roots`.
- **rustls-tls-manual-roots**: Enables TLS functionality provided by- `rustls`, without setting any root certificates. Roots have to be specified manually.
- **rustls-tls-webpki-roots**: Enables TLS functionality provided by- `rustls`, while using root certificates from the- `webpki-roots`crate.
- **rustls-tls-native-roots**: Enables TLS functionality provided by- `rustls`, while using root certificates from the- `rustls-native-certs`crate.
- **blocking**: Provides the- [blocking](https://docs.rs/blocking/index.html)client API.
- **charset**- *(enabled by default)*: Improved support for decoding text.
- **cookies**: Provides cookie session support.
- **gzip**: Provides response body gzip decompression.
- **brotli**: Provides response body brotli decompression.
- **zstd**: Provides response body zstd decompression.
- **deflate**: Provides response body deflate decompression.
- **json**: Provides serialization and deserialization for JSON bodies.
- **multipart**: Provides functionality for multipart forms.
- **stream**: Adds support for- `futures::Stream`.
- **socks**: Provides SOCKS5 proxy support.
- **hickory-dns**: Enables a hickory-dns async resolver instead of default threadpool using- `getaddrinfo`.
- **system-proxy**- *(enabled by default)*: Use Windows and macOS system proxy settings automatically.

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable Features

Some feature flags require additional opt-in by the application, by setting
a `reqwest_unstable` flag.

- **http3**- *(unstable)*: Enables support for sending HTTP/3 requests.

These features are unstable, and experimental. Details about them may be changed in patch releases.

You can pass such a flag to the compiler via `.cargo/config`, or
environment variables, such as:

`RUSTFLAGS="--cfg reqwest_unstable" cargo build`[§](https://docs.rs#sponsors)Sponsors

Support this project by becoming a [sponsor](https://seanmonstar.com/sponsor).

# reqwest_middleware - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/reqwest-middleware/^0.4.2/

## Expand description

This crate provides [ ClientWithMiddleware](https://docs.rs/struct.ClientWithMiddleware.html), a wrapper around

[with the ability to attach middleware which runs on every request.](https://docs.rs/reqwest/0.12.23/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/reqwest/async_impl/client/struct.Client.html)

`reqwest::Client`You’ll want to instantiate [ ClientWithMiddleware](https://docs.rs/struct.ClientWithMiddleware.html) using

[, then you can attach your middleware using](https://docs.rs/struct.ClientBuilder.html)

`ClientBuilder`[, finalize it with](https://docs.rs/struct.ClientBuilder.html#method.with)

`with`[and from then on sending requests is the same as with reqwest:](https://docs.rs/struct.ClientBuilder.html#method.build)

`build````
use reqwest::{Client, Request, Response};
use reqwest_middleware::{ClientBuilder, Middleware, Next, Result};
use http::Extensions;
struct LoggingMiddleware;
#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl Middleware for LoggingMiddleware {
    async fn handle(
        &self,
        req: Request,
        extensions: &mut Extensions,
        next: Next<'_>,
    ) -> Result<Response> {
        println!("Request started {:?}", req);
        let res = next.run(req, extensions).await;
        println!("Result: {:?}", res);
        res
    }
}
async fn run() {
    let reqwest_client = Client::builder().build().unwrap();
    let client = ClientBuilder::new(reqwest_client)
        .with(LoggingMiddleware)
        .build();
    let resp = client.get("https://truelayer.com").send().await.unwrap();
    println!("TrueLayer page HTML: {}", resp.text().await.unwrap());
}
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [reqwest](https://docs.rs/reqwest/0.12.23/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/reqwest/index.html);

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Client](https://docs.rs/struct.ClientBuilder.html)- Builder
- A `ClientBuilder`is used to build a`ClientWithMiddleware`
- [Client](https://docs.rs/struct.ClientWithMiddleware.html)- With - Middleware
- `ClientWithMiddleware`is a wrapper around- `reqwest::Client`
- [Extension](https://docs.rs/struct.Extension.html)
- A middleware that inserts the value into the `Extensions`
- [Next](https://docs.rs/struct.Next.html)
- Next encapsulates the remaining middleware chain to run in `Middleware::handle``run`
- [Request](https://docs.rs/struct.RequestBuilder.html)- Builder
- This is a wrapper around `reqwest::RequestBuilder`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- When attached to a `ClientWithMiddleware``with`
